facts.text: Genoa got its name in spring 1856, likely to avoid confusion with nearby Stony Ridge, Ohio, after the town was originally called Stony Ridge.
A railroad cut of eleven miles rerouted trains straight to Genoa, turning the village into a limestone hub that shipped Genoa White Lime statewide.
The town hall fell into disrepair by the 1970s, was listed on the National Register in 1976, and restored with a $755,000 federal grant in 1978‑79.
The Genoa Opera Hall, the oldest free‑standing municipal building in Ottawa County, is also on the National Register of Historic Places.
In 1835 Timothy and Cinderella Sherman, with their two‑year‑old son Phillip, became the first European settlers in what is now Clay Township.
The first Genoa school, built in 1851, still stands today as Heritage Hall, the village’s historic town hall.
